title: Math · Grade 1
description: An original starter path: build the idea, work an example, then try it. A focused introduction, ready to grow with your class.
framework: Original introductory mathematics practice; suggested grade placement, not a complete standards syllabus.
sequenceNote: Suggested teaching sequence, not mandated unit order.
alignmentNote: Starter course; not full grade-level coverage.

lessons.title: Build tens
lessons.reading: Ten ones can be grouped into one ten. A two-digit number tells how many tens and extra ones it contains.
lessons.easyReading: Ten ones can be grouped into one ten. A two-digit number tells how many tens and extra ones it contains.
lessons.expertReading: Ten ones can be grouped into one ten. A two-digit number tells how many tens and extra ones it contains. Place value assigns different values to the same digit depending on its position.
lessons.worked: Thirty-four means three tens and four ones: 30 + 4 = 34.
steps: Thirty-four means three tens and four ones: 30 + 4 = 34.

application.prompt: What is two tens and six ones?
application.explanation: 26. Ten ones can be grouped into one ten. A two-digit number tells how many tens and extra ones it contains.

lessons.practice: Explain how ten helps solve the question. Include the numbers or properties that support your answer.
lessons.reflection: 26. Ten ones can be grouped into one ten. A two-digit number tells how many tens and extra ones it contains.

lessons.title: Make ten to add
lessons.reading: Split a number to complete ten first. Ten is a useful stopping point because it makes the remaining addition easier.
lessons.easyReading: Split a number to complete ten first. Ten is a useful stopping point because it makes the remaining addition easier.
lessons.expertReading: Split a number to complete ten first. Ten is a useful stopping point because it makes the remaining addition easier. Decomposing an addend uses the associative property to regroup the sum.
lessons.worked: For 8 + 5, split 5 into 2 and 3. Then 8 + 2 = 10 and 10 + 3 = 13.

application.explanation: 13. Split a number to complete ten first. Ten is a useful stopping point because it makes the remaining addition easier.

vocab.definition: Split a quantity into smaller parts without changing its total.

lessons.practice: Explain how decompose helps solve the question. Include the numbers or properties that support your answer.
lessons.reflection: 13. Split a number to complete ten first. Ten is a useful stopping point because it makes the remaining addition easier.

lessons.title: Find the missing part
lessons.reading: Subtraction can ask for a missing part. Think about the addition fact that combines the known part with the missing part.
lessons.easyReading: Subtraction can ask for a missing part. Think about the addition fact that combines the known part with the missing part.
lessons.expertReading: Subtraction can ask for a missing part. Think about the addition fact that combines the known part with the missing part. Addition and subtraction are inverse operations.
lessons.worked: For 12 − 5, ask 5 + what = 12. The missing part is 7.

application.explanation: 8. Subtraction can ask for a missing part. Think about the addition fact that combines the known part with the missing part.

vocab.definition: The result of subtracting one quantity from another.

lessons.practice: Explain how difference helps solve the question. Include the numbers or properties that support your answer.
lessons.reflection: 8. Subtraction can ask for a missing part. Think about the addition fact that combines the known part with the missing part.

lessons.title: Equal means balanced
lessons.reading: An equals sign says both sides have the same value. It does not mean that an answer must always appear on the right.
lessons.easyReading: An equals sign says both sides have the same value. It does not mean that an answer must always appear on the right.
lessons.expertReading: An equals sign says both sides have the same value. It does not mean that an answer must always appear on the right. Equivalent expressions can look different while representing the same quantity.

application.explanation: 3. An equals sign says both sides have the same value. It does not mean that an answer must always appear on the right.

vocab.definition: A statement that two expressions have equal values.

lessons.practice: Explain how equation helps solve the question. Include the numbers or properties that support your answer.
lessons.reflection: 3. An equals sign says both sides have the same value. It does not mean that an answer must always appear on the right.

lessons.title: Measure with equal units
lessons.reading: Repeat equal-sized units without gaps or overlaps. The number of units gives a measurement relative to the chosen unit.
lessons.easyReading: Repeat equal-sized units without gaps or overlaps. The number of units gives a measurement relative to the chosen unit.
lessons.expertReading: Repeat equal-sized units without gaps or overlaps. The number of units gives a measurement relative to the chosen unit. Smaller units usually give a larger numerical measurement of the same length.
lessons.worked: A pencil spans six same-sized cubes placed edge to edge, so its length is six cube lengths.
steps: A pencil spans six same-sized cubes placed edge to edge, so its length is six cube lengths.

application.prompt: Which makes a fair length measurement?
application.explanation: Equal units placed without gaps. Repeat equal-sized units without gaps or overlaps. The number of units gives a measurement relative to the chosen unit.

vocab.definition: The distance from one end of an object to the other.

lessons.practice: Explain how length helps solve the question. Include the numbers or properties that support your answer.
lessons.reflection: Equal units placed without gaps. Repeat equal-sized units without gaps or overlaps. The number of units gives a measurement relative to the chosen unit.
